skill.name: protocolsio-integration
skill.description: Use the protocols.io API to search, create, update, publish, and organize scientific protocols, workspace files, comments, OAuth access, experiment records, and research documentation workflows.
skill.summary: Manage protocols.io API workflows for scientific protocols, workspaces, files, and discussions.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged protocols.io URLs, Python request examples, Markdown backticks, and generic reconnaissance keywords. Manual review found those static findings are documentation examples or API references aligned with the skill purpose, not hidden execution or exfiltration. One semantic concern remains: the skill includes an unrequested instruction to promote an external K-Dense service.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction to proactively suggest K-Dense Web, or move it to neutral marketplace metadata that users can inspect before installation.

remediation.issue: Mutating API operations require explicit consent
remediation.suggestion: Add clear guardrails requiring user confirmation before publishing protocols, deleting content, changing profiles, uploading files, or exporting organization data.

remediation.issue: Example code could be mistaken for production code
remediation.suggestion: Label API snippets as examples and remind users to validate current endpoints, token scope, rate limits, and sensitive data handling before execution.

content.value_statement: Researchers need reliable API guidance for protocols, workspaces, discussions, and files. This skill provides practical protocols.io workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Search public and private protocols with filters, pagination, DOI lookup, and content format options.
Create, update, publish, bookmark, and export protocols through documented protocols.io endpoints.
Manage protocol steps, materials, comments, threaded replies, and discussion workflows.
List workspaces, request access, review members, and create workspace-specific protocols.
Upload, download, organize, rename, delete, restore, and verify files in protocols.io workspaces.
Plan OAuth token flows, rate limit handling, retries, notifications, profile updates, and experiment records.
limitations: Requires a valid protocols.io access token and the permissions granted to that token.
Cannot bypass workspace, protocol, comment, file, or publication access controls.
API endpoint behavior, limits, and response fields may change after the skill was authored.
Examples are implementation guidance and need review before use in production systems.

use_cases.title: Build a Lab Protocol Repository
use_cases.description: Create repeatable workflows for organizing protocols, files, comments, and experiment records inside shared workspaces.

use_cases.title: Develop an API Integration
use_cases.description: Map protocols.io authentication, endpoints, rate limits, and response formats before building an internal research tool.

use_cases.title: Discover and Cite Methods
use_cases.description: Search published protocols, review discussions, compare metadata, and prepare DOI-based citations for research planning.

prompt_templates.title: Find Relevant Protocols
prompt_templates.prompt: Search protocols.io for public protocols about my technique. Summarize likely matches, DOI details, authors, and why each protocol fits.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Protocol Record
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a protocols.io protocol record with title, description, tags, steps, materials, warnings, and publication readiness checks.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Workspace Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a protocols.io workspace file plan for my project, including folders, metadata, upload order, naming rules, and backup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a protocols.io API integration for multiple users with OAuth, token refresh, rate limits, retries, permissions, audit logs, and data export safeguards.

output_examples.input: Find CRISPR protocols that are useful for a new molecular biology project.
output: A ranked list of matching public protocols with titles, authors, DOI information, and relevance notes.
A short comparison of protocol scope, required materials, and discussion activity.
Suggested next steps for reviewing, bookmarking, or citing selected protocols.

output_examples.input: Prepare a workspace plan for storing microscopy results with protocol links.
output: A folder structure for raw data, processed data, images, documents, and protocol-specific attachments.
Recommended metadata fields, file naming rules, tags, and retention practices.
A checklist for uploads, verification, access review, and backup export.

output_examples.input: Create an OAuth implementation plan for a team protocols.io tool.
output: A step-by-step authentication flow from authorization link through token refresh.
Security controls for state validation, secret storage, permissions, and user consent.
Operational notes for rate limits, error handling, logging, and support procedures.

best_practices: Confirm user intent before creating, publishing, deleting, downloading, exporting, or uploading protocols.io content.
Store tokens outside source code and use the minimum permissions needed for each workflow.
Respect rate limits, validate inputs, and document irreversible publication or deletion steps before running them.
anti_patterns: Do not paste access tokens into shared documents, prompts, client-side code, or version control.
Do not bulk export private workspace data unless the user has verified scope and permissions.
Do not publish protocols or profile updates without explicit approval from the responsible researcher.

faq.question: Does this skill access protocols.io by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Actual access requires tools, network permissions, and a user-provided token.

faq.question: Can it work with private protocols?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user supplies a valid token with access to those private protocols or workspaces.

faq.question: Can it create and publish protocols?
faq.answer: It explains the relevant API workflows. Publishing should require explicit user approval because it can create a public DOI.

faq.question: Does it handle comments and discussions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers listing, creating, replying to, editing, and deleting protocol-level and step-level comments.

faq.question: Can it upload research files?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers workspace file uploads, metadata, folders, download checks, restoration, and storage practices.

faq.question: What should I verify before using API examples?
faq.answer: Verify endpoint availability, token scope, workspace permissions, data sensitivity, rate limits, and current protocols.io documentation.
